text:
ashley: spinning up cassini13b-int4 for a limited canary. hitting sporadic OOMs on 2/8 GPUs under mixed traffic. attaching a short log snippet — looks like fragmentation combined with large max_new_tokens. anyone run into this pattern?

sam: share the error and the canary config pls. microbatch settings?

ashley: log:
```
2024-04-02T15:03:21Z cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
server: evicting KV cache: total_slots=32768 used=31240 free=2028
prefetch: queued=24 burst=8 batch_window_ms=12
route-default: max_new_tokens=1024
```
Config was batch_window_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=4096, adaptive_window=false, prefetch=on (heuristic). Canary traffic includes long streaming chats and short single-turn calls.

denise: 1024 is risky for int4 on 13B. Even though memory per token is smaller, allocator fragmentation spikes under sustained allocate/free. Quick mitigations:
- lower default max_new_tokens to 512 for the canary route
- add slot_reserve (e.g., 5%) to avoid immediate thrash during bursts
- tighten evict thresholds to reduce churn

yuri: ditto. We hit something similar with another int4 13B during streaming workloads. Our playbook: soft-cap long sessions, soft-start new sessions (small initial token cap), and a fallback variant (int8) for long outputs. Also reduced prefetch for a test window.

ashley: repro plan:
- set max_new_tokens=512
- batch_window_ms=8
- temporarily disable prefetch for 30m
- enable slot_reserve=0.05 and evict_threshold=0.75

sam: run quick A/B on quality too — quant kernels + different eviction behavior can shift latency or rare output changes. Any eval deltas after quant?

ashley: small perf hit on long-output perplexity: +1.6% on our summarization suite. Short responses fine.

denise: expected. For production we should route long-output requests to an int8 fallback or mixed-precision path > ~600 tokens. That can be automated with a routing rule.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary started for cassini13b-int4 by @ashley at 2024-04-02T15:00:00Z. Dashboard: /canaries/cassini13b-int4

yuri: sample route override for the canary:
```yaml
routes:
  cassini-chat:
    model_variant: cassini13b-int4
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 512
      batch_window_ms: 8
      prefetch: false
      slot_reserve: 0.05
      evict_threshold: 0.75
    fallbacks:
      - cassini13b-int8: 0.1
```
This keeps cost benefits while routing obvious long jobs to int8.

ashley: ran those changes for 45m on mixed canary traffic. Results:
- OOMs down from ~12/hr to ~1/hr
- p50 latency slightly better (smaller batch window), p95 similar
- eval short-task quality unchanged; long-output perplexity delta now +1.3%
- allocator traces show fewer big free/alloc spikes with prefetch off

sam: good. next steps:
1) maintain these defaults for 24h staged canary
2) add per-route token histograms and auto-routing for sessions requesting >512 tokens to int8 fallback
3) implement eval gating: if production long-output perplexity delta > 2% then pause canary

denise: I'll open a small PR: route override + fallback + unit test simulating a streaming 1000-token session. Also updating model-onboarding checklist with "frag-sensitive" kernel note and recommend conservative max_new_tokens by default.

yuri: left allocator snapshot traces in the canary dashboard: /infra/traces/cassini13b/alloc-20240402

ashley: posting metrics to the canary channel. Locking for now unless regression appears. :thumbsup:
